rewrites.summary:
A July 2026 national data analysis places Georgia’s recorded killing rate for trans women at 4.8 per 100k per year — among the country’s highest — and a state law-review article documents a long-run fatality concentration around the city of Atlanta: at least 15 fatal cases statewide across 1990–2014 (11 in Atlanta) and 16 more across 2015–2023 (8 in Atlanta), both series treated by their authors as undercount floors; the analysis’s warning is that a legal-risk grade describes how the state behaves, not how its people do, and Georgia’s documented danger to trans people has been violence on the street more than legislation from the legislature.

On the legal side, licensed medical professionals may not provide patients under 18 with hormone therapy or surgery related to gender transition — the law has applied since 1 July 2023, licence revocation is a possible penalty, and minors who began hormone replacement therapy before that date may continue — and adult gender-affirming surgery access has shrunk: a medical centre in Savannah cancelled all gender-affirming surgeries on 13 February 2025 citing state and national law.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: National policy turbulence and litigation flux colour the legal picture: the 28 January 2025 national executive order denying Medicare and Medicaid funding to providers of youth gender-transition care is what the Savannah medical centre cited over the February 2025 cancellation; a national court settlement (October 2023) requires the state’s public-employee health plan to pay for medically necessary gender-affirming care for employees, spouses and dependents after a December 2022 lawsuit, potentially funding such care for minors outside the state even though it is prohibited inside it; and the minors-care ban, signed on 23 March 2023, drew a promised lawsuit from the state’s civil-liberties organisation.
rewrites.localsOnly: The resident discrimination record includes the April 2023 Atlanta police investigation of three violent crimes against transgender women that year — two Black transgender women were fatally shot a week apart, while a January 2023 shooting that left a transgender woman in critical condition remained open — and the department’s own acknowledgement of the “epidemic-level violence” black and brown transgender women face. For residents, public-employee coverage for gender-affirming care continued under the October 2023 settlement, and at least two other Savannah-area residents were denied care after the February 2025 cancellation.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes: Both killing-count series are acknowledged undercounts, so the true totals and the true rate for trans women are unknown. The February 2025 surgery cancellation was attributed to state and national law, but the link to the 28 January 2025 national funding order is reported as an appearance (“appears to reference”) rather than a published explanation from the medical centre. This record contains no border-screening or document-procedure information for visitors.

blindSourceSummaries: A national data analysis overlaying legal-risk records on recorded homicide data argues that legal risk predicts how the state/province treats you, not how people do; this state/province’s recorded killing rate for trans women is 4.8 per 100k per year — all counts acknowledged as floors from an undercounted monitoring project.

The chief executive signed a 2023 law barring licensed medical professionals from providing patients under 18 with hormone therapy or surgery related to gender transition, with licence revocation as a possible penalty; minors who began hormone replacement therapy before 1 July 2023 may continue. The law took effect 1 July 2023 and the state/province’s civil-liberties organisation said it would sue.

A 2023 national court settlement requires the public-employee health plan to pay for medically necessary gender-affirming care for employees, spouses and dependents, after a 2022 lawsuit argued the plan illegally discriminated by refusing to pay; the plan could be required to pay for care for minors outside the state/province even though it is prohibited inside it.

Police in a major city said in 2023 they were actively investigating three violent crimes against transgender women that year, after two transgender women were fatally shot a week apart; a January 2023 shooting that left a transgender woman in critical condition also remained open, and the department acknowledged epidemic-level violence against transgender women.

A regional medical centre abruptly cancelled all gender-affirming surgeries on 13 February 2025 — including a pre-approved double mastectomy for a 24-year-old transgender man — citing state/province and national law in what appears to reference a 28 January 2025 national executive order denying funding to providers of youth gender-transition care; a community group said at least two other area residents were also denied care.
